A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SKEL-CF. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite dataset renaming and extensive figure relocation.

before.justification: v4 reports original SKEL-CF benchmark results, component ablations, refinement experiments, and attention analyses in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v5 retains original benchmark and ablation results, including MOYO reconstruction results and supplementary camera-factorization and attention analyses.

M1.justification: The reported auxiliary training objective changes: v4 Equation 5 supervises every decoder layer, whereas v5 sums only over intermediate layers, excluding the final layer already supervised by L_dec. The architecture and fitting approach remain substantially unchanged. This establishes a change in the specified objective, not that experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: HMR-SKEL is the renamed 4DHuman-SKEL dataset, with the same source datasets and AVA exclusion. Evaluation coverage remains 3DPW, Human3.6M, EMDB, SPEC-SYN, MOYO/MOYO-HARD, COCO, and qualitative LSP-ext examples.

E2.justification: The comparison methods are retained. Although v5 adds an explicit HSMR row to Table 4, v4 Section 4.4 already compares HSMR with the baseline trained on the proposed dataset. The refinement variants Full predict. and One layer are renamed Full super. and Looped Decoder without changing their configurations.

E3.justification: The stated evaluation metrics, benchmark settings, model sizes, and training schedule remain unchanged. Both versions construct MOYO-HARD from the middle 50% of Camera #1 sequences, totaling 9,725 images. Newly explained preprocessing and camera inputs document the pipeline rather than establish revised experimental settings.

E4.justification: Two qualitative refinement examples from v4 Figure 5 are omitted. The seven examples from v4 Figure S4 remain, redistributed between v5 Figure 5 and Figure S1. Quantitative refinement ablations, component ablations, and attention/camera-factorization analyses are retained; v5 Table 5 redisplays the existing Table S1 experiment.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and supplementary Tables S1–S2 retain their numerical results. The added HSMR row in v5 Table 4 reports COCO PCK@0.05 of 0.86, conflicting with the retained 0.85 in Table 3. Section 3.1 also changes the qualitative finding about optimizing global orientation/translation from no alignment improvement to worse alignment, and two refinement examples are removed.

T1.justification: Equation 5 substantively revises the auxiliary-loss definition by excluding the final decoder term; this is more than changing L to T. The explicit arguments added to Equations 1 and 4 clarify existing mathematics. Neither version provides formal guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims remain improved SKEL estimation through refined training annotations, camera modeling, and coarse-to-fine refinement, with stronger performance than HSMR and competitive SMPL-based accuracy. Dataset renaming and clearer emphasis on intermediate supervision do not materially alter these contributions or their scope.

C2.justification: v5 Section 4.4 adds a mechanism explanation for the shared-layer decoder's poorer results: reduced representational capacity causes inferior reconstruction and weaker generalization. v4 Appendix S2 reported the degradation and emphasized progressive refinement without this explicit capacity explanation. No substantive limitations discussion is added.

D1.justification: v5 specifies person cropping, full-image focal-length prediction, normalized bounding-box cues, and the lower-body/upper-body/full-body fitting order. It omits v4's neutral-SMPL and axis-angle-to-Euler details. Access instructions also change: the introduction promises release upon publication while the abstract still claims availability, and Appendix S1 replaces the video project-page pointer with folder names. Actual availability cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v5 adds the ALBERT reference to contextualize reuse of a single decoder layer and more explicitly contrasts its supervision strategy with HSMR. The remaining related-work coverage and broad research positioning are retained.

P1.justification: The abstract, introductory method description, and several method paragraphs are rewritten, terminology becomes more explicit about camera intrinsics, and 4DHuman-SKEL becomes HMR-SKEL throughout. The refinement discussion expands, but the main section hierarchy and most narrative content remain intact.

P2.justification: The paper changes from two-column to single-column formatting with substantial figure and table redistribution. Figure 2 is redrawn to expose camera prediction, detection, and geometric inputs; comparison figures move between the main text and supplement; refinement panels are regrouped. Table 4 gains descriptive columns and a baseline row, and Table S1 is also displayed as Table 5. Several tables become considerably smaller.

improvement.justification: The revised Figure 2, expanded pipeline explanation, and clearer loss notation improve understandability. However, v5 removes useful orientation-conversion details, introduces conflicting HSMR PCK values and code-release statements, and reduces table legibility. The benchmark evidence is essentially unchanged. These concrete benefits and drawbacks leave the net quality direction uncertain rather than establish an overall improvement.
